transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-28
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jamie Collins (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Maria Gomez (LumenHealth Procurement), Dr. Alan Pierce (CTO), Sophie Lin (Legal Counsel), Tom Reyes (Head of Security)

Summary (auto): procurement + legal review of MSA/DPA, SLA specifics and pricing approvals.

[00:00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we have the full group, appreciate you all making time. Quick roll call?
[00:00:10] Maria: Maria here, Procurement.
[00:00:12] Alan: Alan, CTO.
[00:00:14] Sophie: Sophie, legal.
[00:00:16] Tom: Tom, security.
[00:00:18] Jamie: Great. Ravi from our engineering team is on as well. I'll hand it off to Ravi to run through the technical pilot scope in a bit, but high level today: finalize outstanding MSA/DPA items, confirm SLA commitments, and land on pricing/PO timing.
[00:01:05] Ravi: Hi all — I'll be fairly brief at first, just to ground the pilot. For the pilot we suggest a 2-week benchmark using a subset of production prompts, target 200 QPS bursts with steady-state 10 QPS, and goal latency p95 sub 450ms for generation on our hosted tier. If you need Dedicated reserved capacity that changes throughput guarantees and pricing.
[00:01:48] Sophie: Quick legal note — we circulated an initial redline of the MSA last week. There are three clauses we're still concerned about: indemnity carve-outs, data residency/processing scope in the DPA, and limitation of liability caps.
[00:02:10] Jamie: Understood. On indemnity we included standard language but can look at narrower carve-outs for regulated PHI flows — though we typically push PHI to Private or Dedicated deployments.
[00:02:35] Tom: For security, we need to confirm KMS integration for customer-managed keys and that audit logs are retained for at least 1 year with ability to export. Also SOC 2 report and pen test summary.
[00:02:55] Ravi: KMS is supported in Private and certain Dedicated options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and can integrate customer KMS via our VPC/private deployment in the pilot if needed. Audit logs are exportable and we can provide schema.
[00:03:30] Maria: From procurement — pricing: we need a clear discount schedule tied to 12 vs 24 month commitments and committed token spend thresholds. Can you send an updated price sheet?
[00:03:50] Jamie: Absolutely, we'll send 3 scenarios: PAYG, 12mo commit, 24mo commit with tiered discounts and committed slots for Dedicated if you choose that route. We'll also outline unit economics for batching and caching assumptions.
[00:04:28] Sophie: On the DPA, data residency — LumenHealth has a requirement that PHI data remains in-region (US-EAST). We need to see explicit commitment in the DPA and auditable assurances.
[00:04:45] Ravi: We can pin region to us-east-1 in Dedicated/Private; hosted has regional routing options but not guaranteed physical separation unless reserved. We'll include an SLA and fallback behavior in the DPA language.
[00:05:20] Alan: One technical question — if we do Dedicated, what's the lead time for GPU provisioning and can we do a bench mode where Redwood runs the pilot on hosted but migrates to Dedicated for scale?
[00:05:37] Ravi: Typical provisioning for Dedicated is 4-6 weeks depending on hardware and procurement. We support a migration path: pilot on hosted with telemetry, then cutover to Dedicated with model pinning. We'll provide a migration checklist.
[00:06:10] Tom: Regarding audit logs, do you log token-level inputs/outputs? We need to be careful about storage of PHI content.
[00:06:23] Jamie: By default we store request/response artifacts for X days per policy; for PHI we recommend using Private deployment or configure log redaction/obfuscation and reduced retention. We'll include options in the security pack.
[00:07:05] Sophie: Liability cap — your standard is damages up to fees paid in last 12 months; for healthcare we need higher cap or carve-outs for gross negligence. Is that negotiable?
[00:07:22] Jamie: We can discuss a higher cap in enterprise agreements; for pilots we normally keep standard but we can flag for legal escalation. We'll propose compromise language in the MSA redline document.
[00:08:00] Maria: Timeline — procurement needs a pricing approval by early August to make the Aug 16 pilot kick-off. Is that feasible?
[00:08:14] Jamie: Yes, target is to have updated pricing and redlines by Aug 2 so you can route internally.
[00:08:30] Ravi: I'll cover the pilot metrics we recommend: token budget per prompt, cold-start latency, warm p95, KV cache hit rates; we'll include an instrumentation plan and a Google sheet for results.
[00:09:05] Alan: For SLA specifics, we need an uptime SLO of 99.9% for critical routes and a latency SLO for 95th percentile under expected load.
[00:09:18] Jamie: We can commit to 99.9% for hosted premium and higher for Dedicated with SLA credits. For latency SLOs we'll provide profile numbers per model; for guaranteed latency you usually need Dedicated.
[00:09:50] Sophie: Also need breach notification timelines in the DPA — 72 hours is our standard.
[00:09:58] Jamie: We commonly do 72-hour notification in enterprise agreements. We'll make sure it's explicit in the DPA.
[00:10:30] Tom: Can you share a sample audit log and SOC2 attestation?
[00:10:36] Ravi: Yes — Jamie will share our security pack which includes SOC2 Type II summary, pen test executive summary, and a sample audit log schema.
[00:11:00] Maria: On pricing, what discounts are achievable at the ARR levels we discussed (we estimated $600k/year)?
[00:11:12] Jamie: At that ARR range we can offer mid-tier enterprise discounts; exact % depends on committed term and whether you take Dedicated reserved capacity. We'll run a few scenarios and include list-to-net comparisons.
[00:11:40] Alan: About model versions — will we be able to pin model versions and have automatic rollbacks if quality regresses?
[00:11:50] Ravi: Yes, model pinning and rollout controls are standard; we also have quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so you can detect regressions and rollback.
[00:12:20] Sophie: Back to indemnity, we might need an explicit PHI carve-out where Redwood assumes liability for processing of PHI only when Redwood is explicitly hosting PHI in Dedicated. Can you add language to that effect?
[00:12:36] Jamie: We can draft that: liability focused on services and deployments that process PHI, with obligations around encryption, access controls, and incident response.
[00:13:05] Maria: Are there any third-party sub processors we should know about for hosting?
[00:13:12] Jamie: We use cloud providers and managed services — list will be included in DPA. We'll highlight any sub-processors that touch data in the pilot environment.
[00:13:45] Tom: On KMS: can you support HSM-backed keys and customer-managed keys in Dedicated?
[00:13:52] Ravi: Yes, Dedicated supports customer KMS/HSM integration. We'll include a technical guide and a short checklist for key rotation policies.
[00:14:20] Jamie: Ok let's talk next steps — we'll share three artifacts: updated pricing, MSA redline with accept/decline table, and security pack. Also Ravi will share pilot runbook.
[00:14:38] Sophie: One procedural note: we'll consolidate legal redlines internally and then have a short follow-up call if there are more than 5 contentious items.
[00:14:50] Jamie: Sounds good. Any other blockers?
[00:15:00] Maria: Procurement will need approval chain: VP procurement and CFO sign-off. If pricing looks good we'll route next week.
[00:15:10] Jamie: Good to know.
[00:20:00] (discussion continues — Jamie and Sophie go line-by-line on 3 MSA sections, minor crosstalk and editing notes omitted)
[00:30:30] Ravi: Quick demo note — for the pilot we'll provide SDK keys, sandbox model endpoints, and a telemetry dashboard. You can create routes and pin models per environment.
[00:33:10] Alan: The telemetry data schema — do you surface token-level cost and latency per call?
[00:33:18] Ravi: Yes, token-level cost and latency per route are in the console. We'll also provide trace hooks for your logs.
[00:38:00] Jamie: Recap — Redwood to deliver: pricing scenarios, MSA redline, security pack; Ravi to deliver pilot runbook and benchmark template. Customer to respond with consolidated redlines and procurement approval timeline.
[00:40:15] Sophie: We'll aim to have legal feedback by Aug 6.
[00:41:05] Maria: Procurement aims to approve by Aug 9 to enable PO the week of Aug 16.
[00:45:00] Tom: One last ask — please include an SLA credit table for downtime and performance issues in the redline so our risk team can quantify.
[00:45:18] Jamie: Will do. We'll include credit schedule for different tiers and for Dedicated.
[00:50:00] Alan: Thanks everyone, helpful call.
[00:50:10] Jamie: Thanks all — we'll follow up in email with artifacts.
[00:50:20] Maria: Thanks.
[00:52:00] (meeting ends)
